items.title: Amazon ECR now supports replication backfill for existing container images
items.content_snippet: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports replication backfill, enabling you to replicate existing images in your private registry to your configured replication registry destinations. Previously, replication only applied to images pushed after the replication configuration was enabled, requiring customers to manually retag images to trigger replication of preexisting images. With replication backfill, you can now replicate your full image catalog to new or existing destination

items.title: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock
items.content_snippet: Today, AWS announces the general availability of OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra on Amazon Bedrock. GPT-6.1 Terra expands the GPT-6 family with a balance of capability, speed, and cost efficiency for everyday workloads. As the newest model in the Terra line, GPT-6.1 Terra combines detailed visual reasoning, accurate computer use, and improved factuality and natural writing over GPT-5.6 Terra, for complex workflows. In OpenAI’s Agents’ Last Exam evaluation, it scored 15 percentage points higher than GPT-5.6

items.title: Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances now supports ModifyVolume API
items.content_snippet: Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances now supports the ModifyVolume API, which lets you change volume size, volume type, IOPS, or throughput in place, without detaching the volume or restarting the instance. Previously, changing storage capacity or performance on a deployed managed instance required rebuilding it. With ModifyVolume, you can increase volume size up to 16,384 GiB, switch between supported Amazon EBS volume types, adjust IOPS for gp3, io1, and io2 volumes, and modify throughput

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio adds light mode support for IDC-based domains
items.content_snippet: Today, AWS announces light mode support in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio for Identity Center (IDC) based domains. Customers can now configure the visual interface mode to match their preference, choosing between dark and light themes. With this launch, customers can set this visual preference in both IAM-based and IDC-based domains. items.title: Amazon Connect Customer expands testing and simulation to validate flow action outcomes
items.content_snippet: Amazon Connect Customer now enables you to validate the outcomes of your customer experience flow actions during testing and simulation. In addition to confirming that an action started, you can now verify the data it returns when it completes, such as a Lambda function response, an Amazon Lex resolved intent, or the variables set by an Agentic CX block. items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now lets you view metrics by customer lifetime value and repeat-caller status
items.content_snippet: Now you can view your metrics across customer segments: customer lifetime value (LTV) and repeat callers. items.content_snippet: “The whole point is I want to hit the ground running.” HashiCorp co-founder Mitchell Hashimoto wraps up his day by putting Codex agents to work. They research the competition, compare tools and prototype features he’s still working out—giving him a head start on the next day’s work. Building with Codex? items.title: AI for Detection and Response | Cloudflare’s Mark Anderson
items.content_snippet: Security teams face a constant stream of vulnerabilities and alerts. Cloudflare’s Mark Anderson describes using AI to automate detection and response so experts can focus on threats that need their judgment. He sees automation from companies like OpenAI as a way to take on routine security work and help teams keep pace.

items.title: Better Sources, Better Presentations | Hebbia on Astra
items.content_snippet: Hebbia’s Kavita Anand explains two areas where Astra improved in the company’s evaluations: selecting the right sources and generating PowerPoint presentations. For bankers and investors working through thousands of documents, both help turn research into information they can use.

items.title: Taking on Harder Problems with Astra | Jump Trading
items.content_snippet: At Jump Trading, Lucas Baker is seeing agents take on broader, less defined work—from building entire services to analyses that run for days across multiple data sources. He describes how AI is becoming part of his team’s everyday work.

items.title: Moving IPO Work Forward with AI | Cooley + OpenAI
items.content_snippet: How can AI help reduce the demands of IPO preparation? Cooley’s Chief Innovation Officer David Wang explains how GO Public, built with OpenAI, helps put substantive work in front of clients sooner and spot issues earlier. People remain responsible for reviewing the output and standing behind the answers.

items.title: Why Cybersecurity Needs AI | Cisco’s Jeetu Patel
items.content_snippet: “It is a prerequisite for staying safe that you must use AI.” Attackers can move at machine speed. Defenders need security controls that can adapt just as quickly. Jeetu Patel, President of Cisco, explains why OpenAI is becoming a core foundation for that work. With capabilities like Daybreak and Astra, Cisco sees an opportunity to make security controls and policies dynamic—and strengthen defenses for the businesses that depend on them. Watch why Cisco is rethinking how defense gets done.

items.content_snippet: In 2020, Citibank accidentally sent about $900 million to Revlon’s lenders instead of an $8 million interest payment, even though the procedure, the warning pop-up and three approvers all did what they were supposed to. John Feminella, who works on AI architecture and engineering at Two Sigma, uses that story to show how to give AI agents real autonomy without locking everything down. items.title: Why Are We Still Governing AI Agents Like Software? - Tim Tyler, Gravitee
items.content_snippet: Nobody would hire a worker with no ID, no manager and shared passwords, yet that's how most companies deploy AI agents. Tim Tyler of Gravitee presents the Agent Accountability framework, which governs agents like a digital workforce in three stages: Assignment (identity, team, a named human sponsor), Alignment (role, mission and least-privilege authority) and Administration (oversight scorecards, guardian agents and step-by-step recourse when agents go off course).
